reference.title: 3 Sec Sumo Squat (female)
reference.listing: Video (8 s); data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main knee extensors: control the 3-second lowering and drive the stand. Stance width did not change quadriceps EMG in two studies (McCaw 1999; Paoli 2009), so the sumo stance keeps them working without raising their demand.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main knee extensors: control the 3-second lowering and drive the stand. Stance width did not change quadriceps EMG in two studies (McCaw 1999; Paoli 2009), so the sumo stance keeps them working without raising their demand.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor; wider stances raised gluteus maximus EMG, including unloaded (Paoli 2009), and raised modelled gluteal force (Sinclair 2022). Works hardest standing up out of the bottom.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor; wider stances raised gluteus maximus EMG, including unloaded (Paoli 2009), and raised modelled gluteal force (Sinclair 2022). Works hardest standing up out of the bottom.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus and longus help extend the hip from the wide, turned-out position. Evidence is mixed (McCaw 1999 found a width effect; Paoli 2009 and Larsen 2021 did not), so the stance works them but does not isolate them.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus and longus help extend the hip from the wide, turned-out position. Evidence is mixed (McCaw 1999 found a width effect; Paoli 2009 and Larsen 2021 did not), so the stance works them but does not isolate them.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the way up; no stance-width effect (Paoli 2009).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the way up; no stance-width effect (Paoli 2009).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Soleus and gastrocnemius control the shin; the wide stance asks less of them than a narrow squat (Larsen 2021).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Soleus and gastrocnemius control the shin; the wide stance asks less of them than a narrow squat (Larsen 2021).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Holds the knee out over the toes; no stance-width effect on its EMG (Paoli 2009; Larsen 2021).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the knee out over the toes; no stance-width effect on its EMG (Paoli 2009; Larsen 2021).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the trunk upright, especially through the slow lowering (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the trunk upright, especially through the slow lowering (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Light brace keeps the ribs down and the trunk stiff; bodyweight load does not call for a full breath hold (clinical opinion).

breathing.pattern: Inhale slowly through the 3-second lowering, brace lightly at the bottom pause, exhale as you stand. No full breath hold is needed at body weight.
breathing.cadence: 3 s down (inhale), about 0.5 s pause (brace), about 1 s up (exhale), then a short reset standing (natural breath)

prescription.tempo: 3-1-1-0: 3 s down, a short pause (about 0.5-1 s), about 1 s up, no pause at the top. About 5 s per rep, inside the 2-8 s range drawn from meta-analytic data (Korakakis 2023).
prescription.timeUnderTension: 10 reps x 5 s = about 50 s per set (within the 20-70 s per set proposed by Wilk 2021, who note no data establish optimal values)
prescription.frequency: 2-3 times a week, or as a warm-up before lower-body training
prescription.progression: Lengthen the pause, add reps, then hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest (goblet) or between the legs

cues.text: Feet about 1.5x shoulder width, toes turned out about 30 degrees, hands clasped at the chest. Ribs down, chest tall, light brace.
Breathe in and sit the hips straight down between the heels: one, two, three. Push the knees out over the toes the whole way.
Pause for a beat with thighs about parallel, trunk upright, heels flat.
Breathe out and drive through the whole foot, squeezing the glutes to stand tall.

mistakes.fix: Count one, two, three out loud; the slow descent is the point of the drill.
Push the knees out over the 2nd-3rd toe; reduce depth until you can hold the alignment. Novices drift more than experienced squatters (Lorenzetti 2018).

mistakes.mistake: Toes pointing straight ahead in a wide stance
mistakes.fix: Turn the toes out to match the knees; a wide stance with 0 degrees toe-out was flagged as an extreme position (Lorenzetti 2018).

mistakes.mistake: Folding forward or hinging like a deadlift
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest tall and the hands at the chest; sit down between the heels, not back.
Keep weight across the whole foot; narrow the stance slightly if the heels rise, and stop descending when they do (ACE).

mistakes.mistake: Stance so wide the feet slide or the groin pulls
mistakes.fix: Bring the feet in to about 1.4x shoulder width and use grippy footwear or a non-slip floor; wide stances push more force sideways into the floor (Sinclair 2022).
Hold the pause for a full beat before standing.

kinematics.norm: About 1.5x shoulder width (reference). Studies' wide stances: 140% of shoulder width (McCaw 1999), 1.7x acromion width (Larsen 2021), 150-200% of trochanter distance (Paoli 2009)
30-45 degrees (reference); 0, 21 and 42 degrees tested, wide stance at 0 degrees flagged as extreme (Lorenzetti 2018; Sinclair 2022)
About 100-120 degrees at thighs-parallel; wide-stance loaded 3RM back squats reached about 119-120 degrees (Larsen 2021); bodyweight target at or slightly above that depth (clinical opinion)
About 110-112 degrees at the bottom of loaded squats with a 46-53 degree trunk lean (Larsen 2021); less with the upright bodyweight trunk (clinical opinion)
Increases as the hips sink; about 33 degrees peak at 42 degrees toe-out vs about 20 degrees at 0 degrees (Sinclair 2022, habitual width)
Upright; about 20-35 degrees suggested for the bodyweight version (clinical opinion). Loaded high-bar wide squats: about 46 degrees (Larsen 2021)
Knee over the 2nd-3rd toe throughout; wider stances reduced knee drift (Lorenzetti 2018; ACE)
3 s lowering (reference); short pause; stand in about 1 s (tempo demos)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Wide stances push more force sideways into the floor: use grippy footwear or a non-slip surface.
No study has tested the bodyweight sumo squat itself; stance and depth guidance is extrapolated from loaded squat studies.
modify: Groin or adductor strain history: narrower stance and less depth; build up over weeks.
Hip pain, hip impingement symptoms or after hip surgery: reduce stance width and depth, or follow the clinician's limits (the wide stance increases hip abduction and rotation).
Knee pain: squat only to a pain-free depth and keep the knee over the toes.
Pregnancy and postpartum: follow clinician guidance on depth and breath-holding.
regressions: Hold a chair or rail for balance.
Squat to a box or bench set at a comfortable height.
Shallower depth or a normal-pace lowering until the alignment is consistent.
progressions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest (goblet) or between the legs.

guides.label: Hips sit down between the heels
